flags: MarineMax entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with affiliates of Safe Harbor Marinas, LLC (a portfolio company of Blackstone Infrastructure Partners L.P.) under which each outstanding share of common stock will convert into the right to receive $53.00 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $1.5 billion.

The Hart-Scott-Rodino Act waiting period applicable to the proposed Merger expired, and all required governmental approvals and clearances under applicable foreign antitrust and foreign direct investment laws were received.
MarineMax held a special meeting of shareholders at which the shareholder approval required under the Merger Agreement was received.

pending_offer.claim: MarineMax entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with affiliates of Safe Harbor Marinas, LLC (a portfolio company of Blackstone Infrastructure Partners L.P.) under which each outstanding share of common stock will convert into the right to receive $53.00 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $1.5 billion.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: MarineMax operates as a recreational boat and yacht retailer, marina operator, and superyacht services company with over 120 locations worldwide, including over 70 retail dealerships across 21 U.S. states and 65 marina and storage locations.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we have over 120 locations worldwide, including over 70 retail dealership locations, some of which include marinas.
Collectively, with the IGY acquisition, as of September 30, 2026, we own or operate 65 marina and storage locations worldwide.
Through our over 70 retail locations in 21 states, we sell new and used recreational boats and related marine products, including engines, trailers, parts, and accessories.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: MarineMax's Retail Operations segment sells new and used recreational boats—at an average new-boat selling price of approximately $341,000 in fiscal 2026—along with engines, trailers, parts, accessories, repair and maintenance, slip and storage rentals, brokerage, and yacht charter services.
quotes: As a result of our emphasis on premium brand boats, our average selling price for a new boat in fiscal 2026 was approximately $341,000, an increase from approximately $339,000 in fiscal 2025, compared with the industry average selling price for calendar 2025 of approximately $93,000 based on industry data published by the National Marine Manufacturers Association.

In addition, we provide repair, maintenance, and slip and storage rentals; we arrange related boat financing, insurance, and extended service contracts; and we offer boat and yacht brokerage sales, and yacht charter services.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: MarineMax does not directly finance customer boat purchases, instead earning commissions and marketing fees by placing third-party loans, extended warranty service contracts, and insurance products for dealership customers and for non-dealership transactions through Newcoast Financial Services.
quotes: We do not directly finance our customers’ boat, motor, or trailer purchases.
We recognize commissions earned by us for placing notes with financial institutions in connection with customer boat financing when we recognize the related boat sales.
Through Newcoast Financial Services, we provide third-party financing and insurance products for boats and yachts primarily for transactions not associated with our dealership locations.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Through its Product Manufacturing segment (Cruisers Yachts, Aviara, and Intrepid Powerboats), MarineMax manufactures sport yachts, luxury dayboats, and customized boats for sale through both select MarineMax dealerships and independent dealers.
quotes: Cruisers Yachts, Aviara luxury dayboats, and Intrepid Powerboats all manufacture boats and yachts and recognize sales through our select retail dealership locations and through independent dealers.
As of September 30, 2026, the Product Manufacturing segment includes activity of Cruisers Yachts and Intrepid Powerboats.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Segment Financial Information table of the fiscal 2026 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K) and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: In fiscal 2026, Retail Operations generated $2,158,767 (table in thousands) in revenue and $58,912 (table in thousands) in income from operations, while Product Manufacturing generated 108,632 (table in thousands) in revenue and a (13,653) (table in thousands) operating loss alongside (103,410) (table in thousands) in intersegment revenue eliminations.
quotes: Product Manufacturing | 30,040 | 33,356 | 108,632 | 138,947
The Retail Operations segment includes the majority of all corporate costs.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: While MarineMax operates marinas and superyacht services across the Americas, the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia, its dealership revenue is heavily concentrated in Florida, which accounted for approximately 52%, 54%, and 53% of dealership revenue in fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
quotes: It offers a global network of marinas in the Americas, the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia, delivering year-round accommodations.

Economic conditions in areas in which we operate dealerships, particularly Florida where we generated approximately 52%, 54%, and 53% of our dealership revenue during fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively, can have a major impact on our operations.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1 and Item 1A of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: MarineMax's boat sales depend heavily on a small number of manufacturers—with new Brunswick boats (including 9% Sea Ray and 10% Boston Whaler) representing approximately 20% and Azimut representing approximately 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue—under dealer agreements that grant manufacturers substantial control over territories, pricing, and ownership changes.
quotes: Approximately 20% of our revenue in fiscal 2026 resulted from sales of new boats manufactured by Brunswick, including approximately 9% from Brunswick’s Sea Ray division, 10% from Brunswick’s Boston Whaler division, and approximately 1% from Brunswick’s other divisions.
Additionally, approximately 6% of our revenue in fiscal 2026 resulted from sales of new boats manufactured by Azimut-Benetti Group.

Through these dealer agreements, boat manufacturers (particularly Brunswick and Azimut) exercise significant control over their dealers, restricting them to specified locations, and retaining approval rights over changes in management and ownership, among other things.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by discretionary consumer spending, interest rates affecting boat financing, economic confidence, and geopolitical or trade conditions; in fiscal 2026, revenue declined 6.3% to approximately $2.164 billion from $2.309 billion in fiscal 2025 due to a 6% decrease in comparable-store sales and lower manufacturing and closed-store sales.
quotes: Revenue decreased $145.3 million, or 6.3%, to approximately $2.164 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 from $2.309 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025.

The comparable-store decrease was primarily driven by decreases in new and used boat revenue as a result of the challenging retail environment, ongoing economic uncertainty, evolving trade policies and geopolitical tensions, including the Iran conflict.

Additionally, the Federal Reserve's increases of its benchmark interest rate resulted in significantly higher long-term interest rates, which negatively impacted, and may continue to negatively impact, our customers’ willingness or desire to purchase our products.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Outside Florida, business seasonality generates lower sales and higher inventories and short-term borrowings in the December and March quarters—averaging 22% and 25% of annual revenue versus 29% and 24% in the June and September quarters—while January boat shows and weather patterns affect demand.
quotes: Over the three-year period ended September 30, 2026, the average revenue for the quarterly periods ended December 31, March 31, June 30 and September 30 represented approximately 22%, 25%, 29%, and 24%, respectively, of our average annual revenue.

The onset of the public boat and recreation shows in January generally stimulates boat sales and allows us to reduce our inventory levels and related short-term borrowings throughout the remainder of the fiscal year.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K and the fiscal 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: Gross margin is driven by boat profitability, business mix shifts toward higher-margin non-boat operations such as marinas and parts and service, tariff refunds, and manufacturer rebates and dealer incentives, expanding gross margin to 34.9% in fiscal 2026 from 32.5% in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Gross profit as a percentage of revenue increased to 34.9% for the twelve months ended September 30, 2026 from 32.5% for the twelve months ended September 30, 2025.

The increase in gross profit as a percentage of revenue was attributable to modest improvements in boat margins, a greater mix of sales from our higher margin businesses, and to a lesser degree tariff refunds received related to boat sales.
The failure to receive rebates and other dealer incentives (interest assistance and co-op assistance) on inventory purchases or retail sales could substantially reduce our margins.

business_model.basis: Stated in Item 1A and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K and the Supplemental Financial Information table in the fiscal 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative expenses rose 8.6% to $702.9 million (32.5% of revenue) in fiscal 2026 from $647.2 million (28.0% of revenue) in fiscal 2025, driven by a greater mix of higher-margin businesses with higher expense structures and transaction costs (including 25,854 (table in thousands) in transaction and other costs), alongside a fixed cost base.
quotes: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $55.7 million, or 8.6%, to $702.9 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 from $647.2 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025.

The increase in selling, general, and administrative expenses was driven by an increase in mix to our higher margin businesses, which typically carry a higher expense structure, and increased transaction and other related costs.
We have a fixed cost base that can affect our profitability if demand decreases.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Consolidated Balance Sheets and Item 7 of the fiscal 2026 Form 10-K, and the fiscal 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: MarineMax finances inventory with short-term floor-plan borrowings (613,671 (table in thousands) at fiscal 2026 year-end versus 715,679 (table in thousands) a year earlier), and reducing inventories by $54.6 million along with lower interest rates reduced interest expense by $13.2 million to $58.0 million in fiscal 2026.
quotes: Short-term borrowings (Floor Plan) | 613,671 | 715,679
The decrease in interest expense was primarily the result of decreased borrowings from lower inventory levels and lower interest rates.

Inventories declined $54.6 million, or 6.3%, to $812.8 million in fiscal 2026 from $867.3 million at the end of fiscal 2025, which followed a $39.3 million decline in inventory from the end of fiscal 2024.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1] as management's belief and reported facility counts as of September 30, 2026.
competitive_position.claim: MarineMax describes itself as the world's largest recreational boat and yacht retailer, marina operator, and superyacht services company, with over 120 locations worldwide, over 70 retail dealership locations, and 65 marina and storage locations.
quotes: We believe we are the world’s largest recreational boat and yacht retailer, marina operator and superyacht services company.
As of September 30, 2026, we have over 120 locations worldwide, including over 70 retail dealership locations, some of which include marinas.
Collectively, with the IGY acquisition, as of September 30, 2026, we own or operate 65 marina and storage locations worldwide.

competitive_position.claim: MarineMax operates what it believes to be the only global luxury marina network through IGY Marinas and the largest superyacht services provider through Fraser Yachts and Northrop & Johnson.
quotes: Through Fraser Yachts and Northrop & Johnson, we believe we are the largest superyacht services provider, operating locations across the globe.
IGY Marinas (“IGY”), which we believe to be the only global marina operator, provides a network of marina locations across the Americas, the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1] and [P3] business and strategy descriptions.
competitive_position.claim: MarineMax operates a vertically integrated marine model spanning boat manufacturing, dealership retail, brokerage, finance and insurance, marinas, yacht charters, and proprietary digital platforms.
quotes: Many of our revenue streams, including IGY, reinforce our vertically integrated model and allow us to support customers across the entire recreational marine value chain.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1], citing company fiscal 2025–2026 figures and National Marine Manufacturers Association calendar 2025 data.
competitive_position.claim: MarineMax emphasizes premium brands, achieving a fiscal 2026 new-boat average selling price of approximately $341,000 (up from $339,000 in fiscal 2025) compared with the industry calendar 2025 average of approximately $93,000.
quotes: As a result of our emphasis on premium brand boats, our average selling price for a new boat in fiscal 2026 was approximately $341,000, an increase from approximately $339,000 in fiscal 2025, compared with the industry average selling price for calendar 2025 of approximately $93,000 based on industry data published by the National Marine Manufacturers Association.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1] and [P2] descriptions of dealer agreements.
competitive_position.claim: MarineMax holds exclusive geographic dealer rights for Sea Ray and Boston Whaler in almost all of its markets, exclusive U.S. dealer rights for Azimut, and multi-year Brunswick agreements providing the lowest domestic dealer prices.
quotes: We have agreements with Brunswick covering Sea Ray products and Boston Whaler products and are the exclusive dealer of Sea Ray and Boston Whaler boats in almost all of our geographic markets.
We also are the exclusive dealer for Italy-based Azimut-Benetti Group, or Azimut, for Azimut and Benetti mega-yachts, yachts, and other recreational boats for the United States.

Most of our retail locations have a multi-year dealer agreement which provides for the lowest product prices charged by the Sea Ray division of Brunswick or Boston Whaler, as applicable, from time to time to other domestic Sea Ray or Boston Whaler dealers, as applicable.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P4] CEO commentary and [P3] financial results table and discussion.
competitive_position.claim: Expanding higher-margin, non-boat revenue streams since 2019 contributed to gross margin expansion from 26.1% in fiscal 2019 to 34.9% in fiscal 2026, up from 32.5% in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Since 2019, we have expanded our higher-margin, non-boat revenue streams, contributing to a significant improvement in gross margin from 26.1% in fiscal 2019 to 34.9% in fiscal 2026.
Gross profit as a percentage of revenue increased to 34.9% for the twelve months ended September 30, 2026 from 32.5% for the twelve months ended September 30, 2025.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1] operating metrics and store-closure disclosures and [P3] MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Although management believes MarineMax gains market share during weak markets, same-store sales decreased 2% in fiscal 2025 and 5% in fiscal 2026, revenue fell 6.3% to $2.164 billion in fiscal 2026, and 11 retail locations were closed during the last three fiscal years.
quotes: Although past economic conditions have adversely affected our operating results, we believe during and after such conditions we have capitalized on our core strengths to substantially outperform the industry, resulting in market share gains.
Our same-store sales increased 1% in fiscal 2024, decreased 2% in fiscal 2025, and decreased 5% in fiscal 2026.
Revenue decreased $145.3 million, or 6.3%, to approximately $2.164 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 from $2.309 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P3] goodwill discussion and [P4] segment financial information table.

quotes: As a result of the declining performance of the product manufacturing reporting unit and segment the Company recognized a non-cash, pre-tax goodwill impairment charge of $69.1 million related to the product manufacturing reporting unit.
There was no remaining carrying value of the goodwill for the product manufacturing reporting unit and segment as of June 30, 2025 as a result of the goodwill impairment.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1] revenue concentration disclosures and [P2] Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: MarineMax relies heavily on Brunswick (approximately 20% of fiscal 2026 revenue, plus Mercury Marine engines) and Azimut (approximately 6% of fiscal 2026 revenue), and boat manufacturers exercise substantial control over dealer locations, ownership changes, and acquisitions.
quotes: Sales of new Brunswick boats accounted for approximately 20% of our revenue in fiscal 2026.
Sales of new Azimut boats and yachts accounted for approximately 6% of our revenue in fiscal 2026.
Substantially all of our products are powered with outboard engines from Mercury Marine, Yamaha, and inboard engines from Volvo, which makes us reliant on these companies for the supply of engines.

Through these dealer agreements, boat manufacturers (particularly Brunswick and Azimut) exercise significant control over their dealers, restricting them to specified locations, and retaining approval rights over changes in management and ownership, among other things.

competitive_position.claim: MarineMax depends on manufacturer rebates, interest assistance, and co-op assistance programs, whose reduction or elimination could increase inventory costs and substantially reduce margins.
quotes: The failure to receive rebates and other dealer incentives (interest assistance and co-op assistance) on inventory purchases or retail sales could substantially reduce our margins.

competitive_position.claim: MarineMax faces intense competition for customers, products, boat show space, and retail locations in a highly fragmented recreational boat industry, alongside growing competitive importance of digital channels and alternative leisure spending.
quotes: In addition to facing competition generally from recreation businesses seeking to attract consumers’ leisure time and discretionary spending dollars, the recreational boat industry itself is highly fragmented, resulting in intense competition for customers, quality products, boat show space, and suitable retail locations.
In addition to our traditional repeat and referral business in our physical locations, digital channels are increasingly significant in serving our existing customer base and reaching new customers.
Our continued expansion and success will be negatively impacted if we are not able to fully exploit these channels.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P2] Risk Factors and [P3] MD&A.
competitive_position.claim: Higher long-term interest rates, economic uncertainty, inflation, tariffs, and geopolitical conflicts threaten demand for MarineMax's discretionary products, while its fixed cost base and inventory financing needs heighten margin and supply risks.
quotes: Additionally, the Federal Reserve's increases of its benchmark interest rate resulted in significantly higher long-term interest rates, which negatively impacted, and may continue to negatively impact, our customers’ willingness or desire to purchase our products.
We have a fixed cost base that can affect our profitability if demand decreases.
The availability and costs of borrowed funds can adversely affect our ability to obtain adequate boat inventory and the ability and willingness of our customers to finance boat purchases.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P3] MD&A and [P2] Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: MarineMax is heavily concentrated in Florida, which generated approximately 52% of dealership revenue in fiscal 2026 (54% in fiscal 2025 and 53% in fiscal 2024), exposing operations to regional economic downturns, storms, and environmental disruptions.
quotes: Economic conditions in areas in which we operate dealerships, particularly Florida where we generated approximately 52%, 54%, and 53% of our dealership revenue during fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively, can have a major impact on our operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in [P1] and [P2] Merger disclosures and Risk Factors.
competitive_position.claim: During the pending $53.00 per share cash merger with Safe Harbor Marinas, interim operating covenants restrict MarineMax from pursuing certain business opportunities or competing bids (with a $31,650,000 termination fee under specified conditions), while merger uncertainties risk disrupting OEM, supplier, customer, and employee relationships.
quotes: At the effective time of the Merger (the “Effective Time”), each issued and outstanding share of our common stock, par value $0.001 per share (our “common stock”), as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than those (i) held by MarineMax, or (ii) owned, directly or indirectly, by Parent or Merger Sub) will convert automatically into the right to receive $53.00 per share in cash, without interest thereon and less any required tax withholdings.

These restrictions could prevent us from pursuing certain business opportunities that may arise prior to the consummation of the Merger and may affect our ability to execute our business strategies and attain financial and other goals and may impact our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

The Merger Agreement contains provisions that limit our ability to pursue alternatives to the Merger and that could deter or discourage a competing acquirer from making a favorable alternative transaction proposal.

In addition, upon the termination of the Merger Agreement under specified circumstances, including, among others, the termination by the Parent in the event of an Adverse Recommendation Change (as defined in the Merger Agreement) by our Board of Directors (if at the time of termination neither Parent nor Merger Sub is then in material breach of its representations, warranties, covenants or agreements under the Merger Agreement), we would be required to pay Parent a termination fee of $31,650,000.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1 Business (P1) and the fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year earnings release (P4).
growth_thesis.claim: Since 2019, MarineMax has diversified into higher-margin, non-boat marine businesses through strategic acquisitions, lifting gross margin from 26.1% in fiscal 2019 to 34.9% in fiscal 2026.
quotes: Established in 1998 as a U.S.-based recreational boat and yacht dealership, more recently, starting in 2019, we have broadened our international footprint and diversified our asset portfolio through strategic acquisitions of higher-margin businesses within the marine industry.
Since 2019, we have expanded our higher-margin, non-boat revenue streams, contributing to a significant improvement in gross margin from 26.1% in fiscal 2019 to 34.9% in fiscal 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year earnings release (P4).
growth_thesis.claim: Growth in higher-margin areas including marinas and parts and service partially offset lower boat sales in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.
quotes: The decrease primarily reflected lower boat sales, partially offset by continued growth in several higher-margin areas of the business, including marinas and parts and service.

growth_thesis.claim: Continued acquisition-led growth requires acquiring businesses at attractive or fair prices, integrating operations, and obtaining manufacturer consents such as from Brunswick.
quotes: Our success depends, in part, on our ability to continue to make successful acquisitions at attractive or fair prices and to integrate the operations of acquired dealers and each dealer we acquire in the future.
We may be required to obtain the consent of Brunswick and various other manufacturers prior to the acquisition of other dealers.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1A Risk Factors (P2) and Item 7 MD&A (P3).
growth_thesis.claim: While the Merger Agreement is in effect, interim operating covenants restrict business activities and could prevent MarineMax from pursuing business opportunities, after completing no acquisitions in fiscal 2026.
quotes: These restrictions could prevent us from pursuing certain business opportunities that may arise prior to the consummation of the Merger and may affect our ability to execute our business strategies and attain financial and other goals and may impact our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

We completed three acquisitions in the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024, three acquisitions in the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, and no acquisitions in the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026.

growth_thesis.claim: MarineMax expands product offerings across its over 70 retail locations by adding complementary brands and owned lines to give customers a migration path and support same-store sales.
quotes: We add brands with the intent to either offer a migration path for our existing customer base or fill a gap in our product offerings.
We believe our expanded product offerings have strengthened our same-store sales growth.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 1 Business (P1) and Item 1A Risk Factors (P2).

quotes: Sales of new Brunswick boats accounted for approximately 20% of our revenue in fiscal 2026.
Sales of new Azimut boats and yachts accounted for approximately 6% of our revenue in fiscal 2026.

The failure to obtain a high quality and desirable mix of competitively priced products that our customers demand could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
The failure to receive rebates and other dealer incentives (interest assistance and co-op assistance) on inventory purchases or retail sales could substantially reduce our margins.
